rjzq66.title: Former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect to curb AI clones
rjzq66.content:
Copycat fight.

Image credit: Eurogamer

Former Rockstar Games North technical director Obbe Vermeij believes that the possibility of AI vibe coded ports of Grand Theft Auto 6 could push Rockstar to create an official PC version sooner than you'd expect.
Speaking to RockPaperShotgun as part of a wider interview, Vermeij said generative AI "really has changed the world.". He elaborated: "I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as [the developer's] effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together."

Here's the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6Watch on YouTube

Vermeij emphasised that he doesn't know what Rockstar's plans are, but with his technical expertise, he does believe that generative AI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a GTA 6 PC port.
"It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things," Vermeij said. "And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it.".We've already seen people thrust footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 into AI software over the past few months. AI slop videos have been pulling in millions of views on social media, and people have been 'improving' trailer footage with Nvidia's DLSS5 'yassification' machine (thanks Ars Technica). Grand Theft Auto 6 itself will not feature any generative AI or microtransactions at launch.
AI game clones continue to be a problem. Game developers have cancelled public demos in fear of having their game copied, and Steam owner Valve has gone out to say it's the developer's responsibility to prevent cloning by making their games more original. Even as Anthropic has introduced measures to prevent such practices, other AI software can still perform such tasks.

1tegdc0.title: Phantom Blade Zero Is Now Better on Steam Machine - Steam Deck HQ
1tegdc0.content:
If you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

Phantom Blade Zero is one of my favorite games I’ve played this year, and it’s one of the only games that I’ve given a perfect score in my review. It’s an incredible experience, with an interesting story, unmatched combat, and a rewarding progression system that makes each unique weapon we can use feel even more unique. It’s definitely a game. I highly recommend picking it up, and if you could only pick up a few games, this should be one of them.

However, before yesterday, I wouldn’t have tried playing this on the Steam Deck, and it was a little tough to enjoy on the Steam Machine. I love the game, but it couldn’t hit a stable 30 FPS on the Deck, and there were major slowdowns in later areas. The slowdowns were bad enough that it made it so we could only play at 30 FPS for a stable experience on the Machine. But with a new patch, the performance has changed, and it actually makes it significantly more enjoyable on the Steam Machine.

In the new patch, which was released two days ago, there were a few new audio features and some bug fixes. On top of that, there were also some updates to the shader compilation process to reduce startup times, adjustments to the behavior of certain bosses, and improved performance in certain areas. To me, this translated to improved performance in harder-hitting areas, like Pangzhen, but with how generic the entry is in the patch notes, I didn’t pay as much attention. Well, I still tried it, regardless, and the improvement to the performance is massive.

With how massive this patch has been for performance in general, I was hoping it would have some effect on the Steam Deck. Sadly, a lot of the issues still remain, and there’s no way to play at a stable 30 FPS, even at the lowest possible settings. It still stutters when running around crowded areas, like Pangzhen, and getting into larger fights, sometimes dropping to 20 FPS.

I do hope we will see further optimization that will make it more playable on the Deck, but for now, I would still avoid this one for the device.

Steam Machine

On the Steam Machine, Phantom Blade Zero is performing significantly better in all of the areas that it had trouble in when I reviewed the game. Up until this patch, it still had those performance problems, and it was quite difficult to play at any framerate above 30 FPS if you want a stable experience. However, with those same settings I recommended originally (2K resolution, FSR Balanced, and Medium quality), we can now get almost stable 60 FPS in all of the problem areas.

A lot of the fights that I tested that had those drops before are almost completely stable at 60 FPS. There are still some minor drops to around 57 FPS (51 at the lowest), but it’s negligible and still feels very smooth in the heat of battle. It’s also much more stable when running around crowded areas like Pangzhen, though there are some small drops here and there. It never goes below 50 FPS, but it can feel like there are some minor stutters when running around.

Even so, there’s no doubt that this is a significant improvement over the experience before this patch. It has become significantly more playable all around, and it’s now a game I can easily and happily recommend on the Machine.

Conclusion

It’s sad that Phantom Blade Zero hasn’t gotten better on the Deck, and I hope it does in time, but I am glad to say that it’s much better to play on the Steam Machine now. I felt it was a little too demanding for what was being asked, considering you couldn’t hit 60 FPS on low settings with 1080p resolution before the patch. Now, we can easily hit 60 FPS on Medium settings at 2K resolution, which is a huge difference. With this patch, it’s a no-brainer.

pcjnsd.title: "Is there any accountability left in this world?" Warren Spector pops off at EA executives and their massive payouts as BioWare shuts down
pcjnsd.content:
"Obviously not."

Image credit: Eurogamer

It's only been two weeks since we last heard Warren Spector sound off about EA's sudden decision to close BioWare, following the publisher's acquisition by Saudi Arabia's PIF and venture capitalist concerns. But now, the storied developer is back and - apparently - angrier than ever.
"I recently posted my thoughts about EA’s shuttering of BioWare," Spector wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "Those of you who read my post know that I was unhappy. I remain so. The tragedy of so many layoffs the last few years hasn’t been lost on me, but for some reason, BioWare hit me on an emotional level that nothing before had. I felt gut-punched."
Spector goes on to counter the idea that the studio was closed down as a "sound business decision" because the "studio’s glory days (artistic and commercial) were behind them" and that "businesses don’t succeed on history alone". These reactions, more than anything else, appear to be what's inspired Spector to take to posting again - he simply cannot agree with this assessment.
"If studio-level people leave, resulting in dilution of talent, someone is creating an environment that pushes them out. Do those culture-killers pay any price? If executives misread the market, over-hire, or make decisions that result in under-funded, over-funded, poorly-marketed games do they lose sleep let alone jobs?" he asks."Do those same executives suffer like developers when the needs of financial partners and private investors take precedence over the people who actually create value, let alone over the interests of players? Does anyone up there in or adjacent to the C-suite care? Is there any accountability left in this world? Obviously not."
He then goes on to list the yearly payouts that some of the highest-level executives at EA are rewarded per annum. These include:

Andrew Wilson (chief executive officer): $38.65 million
Laura Miele (president)t: $13.7 million
Stuart Canfield (chief financial officer): $11.3 million
Jake Schatz (chief legal officer): $8.4 million
Mala Singh (chief people officer): $8.3 million

"Tens of thousands of do-ers and makers are out of work and these people think they're worth that kind of compensation?" continues Spector. "And if you think this is a discussion about 'sound business decisions', I hope you never get anywhere near running a business. Or at least that people have the sense not to go work for you."Back in August, we saw Warren Spector announce his intention to retire from the world of video game development. Spector's announcement comes shortly after the last game he worked on - Thick as Thieves - had its final major update only a few months after its release. Despite its charm and low price, Thick as Thieves sadly didn't sell what it needed to, resulting in layoffs at Spector's studio.

1nxnahn.title: «GTA может подождать, а это не может!»: фанаты «Последнего рубежа» остались в восторге от нового геймплея Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4
1nxnahn.content:
Режим «Последний рубеж» (The Last Stand) полюбился фанатам Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 2, но прошёл мимо Dawn of War 3. Разработчики амбициозной стратегии Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 повторять ошибки прошлого не намерены.
Источник изображений: Deep Silver

Издатель Deep Silver и немецкая студия King Art Games (Iron Harvest) в новом выпуске «Отчётов с поля боя» устроили «колоссальную» демонстрацию «Последнего рубежа» в Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
В 30-минутном геймплейном ролике разработчики Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 показали новые механики, возможности персонализации и тактическую глубину, которые ждут игроков в «Последнем рубеже».

Игрокам «Последнего рубежа» в роли могущественных командиров предстоит объединить силы с двумя другими пользователями, чтобы противостоять натиску 20 волн всё более и более сложных врагов.
В Dawn of War 4 командиры будут сражаться не в одиночку: каждый возглавляет ударную группу из четырёх отрядов спутников. «Последний рубеж» стартует с пятью командирами — дополнительные прибудут после релиза в виде DLC.

Зрители остались в восторге от возвращения «Последнего рубежа» и столь масштабной демонстрации режима. «GTA может подождать, а это не может! Дайте мне [игру] сейчас же!» — призвал malarkey0949 разработчиков Dawn of War 4.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 выйдет 3 декабря в Steam, но покупатели премиум-издания получат игру 30 ноября. Обещают эпичный сюжет, четыре фракции, мультиплеер, перевод на русский и масштабную пострелизную поддержку.

1vjipf7.title: After gobbling up EA, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake reportedly looking to buy Unity
1vjipf7.content:
Second course.

After acquiring EA for $55bn earlier this year, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake are reportedly in the market for another massive video game company. And according to new reports, it's Unity.
Per Reuters, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Silver Lake - two major actors in the EA acquisition - are in talks to acquire the video game engine company for around $25bn. Silver Lake's Egon Durban already sits on the Unity Board of Directors, and the firm owns around eight percent of its shares already thanks to a $400m investment.

Here's the video that was released when Unity aquired Weta StudiosWatch on YouTube

This $25bn valuation should be taken with a grain of salt for two core reasons. For one, it was decided prior to Unity's latest quarterly financial report, which included a 59% increase in strategic revenue year-over-year and net income of $122m. So this could propel the valuation upwards.On the other hand, wider economic changes could have a detrimental effect. Reuters points out: "Strong ⁠growth in Unity's AI-powered Vector advertising platform helped it post its first quarterly profit on a GAAP basis since going public in September 2020." Given we've seen the generative AI sector take a major hit this week following the US midterm elections, it's possible companies using the tech may be viewed with more fiscal skepticism. Or, maybe this dip is just temporary. In short, take the $25bn valuation as a ballpark figure.
Unity has had something of an interesting past. There was of course the banana's runtime fee scandal of 2024 in which the company attempted to charge developers a fee on each game sale using the engine, which proved a PR nightmare and was quickly walked back. Unity also recently partnered with Google for AI-game creation platforms Google PlayGround and Unity Spark. Spark is shown to have created a Space Corridor game on its website that looks dubious at best - not exactly a resounding testament to the future.
The last time EA and Silver Lake bought something gaming related it was EA, a Western giant that would go on to lay off hundreds of staff and close BioWare months later. It is worth emphasising that the deal was a leveraged buyout, which saddles EA with substantial debt, whereas the exact nature of this proposed Unity deal is not confirmed. As such if it does happen, it may be a good ol' fashioned private acquisition, not this terms and conditions-laden deal that EA, in its newest guises, must contend with. We've already seen BioWare closed down as a result of this acquisition.
Expect more news about the Unity buyout when official information comes to light.

1b2imo9.title: Unity reports "strongest ever" Q3 results driven by its AI-powered ad network Vector
1b2imo9.content:
Revenue grew 32% year-on-year to $622 million, marking Unity's first GAAP profitable quarter since its IPO in 2020

Unity has delivered its "strongest ever" third quarter results, driven by a 126% year-on-year growth in its AI-powered ad network Vector.
As a result, Unity achieved its first GAAP-profitable quarter since its IPO in 2020.
Meanwhile, reports indicate the company has held acquisition talks with private equity firm Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, both involved in the $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts.
"We are seeing the compounding impact of our flywheel strategy," said Unity CEO and president Matt Bromberg. "More creators make more games on our platform, more games fuel the need for more discovery through advertising."
The numbers

Revenue: $622 million, up 32% year-on-year
Create Solutions revenue: $165 million, up 8% year-on-year
Grow Solutions revenue: $457 million, up 44% year-on-year
GAAP net income: $122 million (with a margin of 20%)

The highlights
Unity's Vector falls under Grow Solutions revenue, which rose 44% year-on-year to $457 million. These results were also partially offset by decreases in its IronSource Ads network, which sunset during the company's second quarter.
Create Solutions revenue grew 8% to $165 million, driven by higher subscription revenue, but was offset by declines in cloud and hosting services following Unity's portfolio reset last year.
"Create Solutions revenue was $165 million, up 8% year-over-year. The increase was driven by increases in subscription revenue, partially offset by decreases in cloud and hosting services revenue, driven by our portfolio reset in 2025"
Strategic revenue was $597 million, up 59% year-on-year. In contrast, non-strategic revenue fell 73% from $95.7 million to $25.5 million.
This primarily consists of revenue from IronSource and mobile publisher Supersonic, which was acquired by Tripledot Studios in August for $40 million.
As for acquisition talks, sources told Reuters that a consortium of investors discussed Unity's $25 billion valuation before the release of the company's latest financial results.
Reuters also reported that the results increased Unity's market capitalisation to an estimated $21.5 billion, with shares rising 4% in extended trading.
"Unity has been working with an investment bank to evaluate its options following the approach," sources told Reuters. "No deal is certain, and the plan and terms may still change."

4ebhwh.title: Первый за пять лет патч «раздул» размер Nier: Automata в Steam с 40 до 366 гигабайт
4ebhwh.content:
Нашумевший постапокалиптический ролевой экшен Nier: Automata от Square Enix и PlatinumGames получил первый за пять лет патч. Вместе с долгожданными нововведениями апдейт обернулся новой головной болью для игроков.
Источник изображения: Square Enix

Накануне Square Enix и PlatinumGames сообщили о выходе для Nier: Automata в цифровом магазине Steam обновления с текстовым переводом на корейский и китайский (традиционный, упрощённый) языки.
Как быстро подметили пользователи сервиса Valve, размер обновления Nier: Automata составил внушительные для столь скромного списка изменений 8 Гбайт, однако это ещё не самое страшное.

Источник изображения: RPGSite

Портал RPGSite обратил внимание, что с новым патчем размер Nier: Automata в Steam увеличился почти в девять раз — с 40,73 Гбайт до 366,56 Гбайт. Проблема связана с вышедшими DLC для игры.
На странице управления дополнительным контентом в библиотеке Steam можно наблюдать (см. изображение выше), что вес каждого DLC для Nier: Automata теперь составляет те же 40,73 Гбайт. Размер основной игры не поменялся.
Источник изображения: Square Enix

Официальный японский микроблог Nier проблему подтвердил и заверил, что решение уже в работе. А пока извинился за доставленные неудобства и посоветовал отключить установку DLC, чтобы загрузить лишь базовую игру.

Nier: Automata вышла в марте 2017 года на PC (Steam, Microsoft Store), PS4 и Xbox One, а осенью 2022-го добралась до Nintendo Switch. Игра заслужила высокие оценки критиков, продалась в объёме 10 млн копий и заработала культовый статус.

197m12p.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
197m12p.content:
Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security, a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source. The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies. 

Palo Alto Networks and Clutch Security did not respond to a request for comment. The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.

The high valuation is not an anomaly in a market increasingly focused on securing software against bad actors using AI to breach systems more easily. Upwind, a startup using AI to secure cloud infrastructure, recently turned down an acquisition offer from Datadog that valued it at roughly 40 times ARR, TechCrunch reported last week.  

If the deal happens, it would be Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition this year, according to PitchBook. The cybersecurity giant has a history of buying innovation rather than building it in-house, and it has ramped up dealmaking this year in response to rising AI-driven cyberattacks.

In September, Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, a two-year-old startup that uses AI agents to automate routine IT help desk tasks. The transaction valued Console at $500 million in stock and cash, TechCrunch reported. Other VC-backed companies that Palo Alto Networks has scooped up this year include NEA-backed Embrace, for $325 million; Chronosphere, an observability platform backed by Greylock and Lux Capital, for $2.95 billion; and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $231 million, according to regulatory filings.

Several of Clutch’s competitors have also been acquired. Cyera, a cybersecurity startup valued at $12 billion earlier this year, acquired Oasis Security, which, like Clutch, focuses on managing AI agents’ access to systems, for $1 billion. Meanwhile, Cisco bought Menlo Ventures-backed Astrix for roughly $400 million, Calcalist reported.

05.11.2026 [23:29], 

Компания Sony в рамках отчёта по итогам предыдущего квартала сообщила, что создание игровой консоли PlayStation 6 продвигается «по графику» и в предстоящем году компания намерена добиться «значительного прогресса». Но компания по-прежнему не готова раскрыть сроки выпуска приставки следующего поколения.
Источник изображений: Sony

Ранее генеральный директор Sony Хироки Тотоки (Hiroki Totoki) заявил журналистам, что компания пока не определилась с датой выпуска PlayStation 6, но «активно инвестирует в новую платформу». Тем не менее, некоторые аналитики ожидают, что консоль появится в 2028 году — уже после того, как PlayStation прекратит продажи игр на физических носителях.
«Для обеспечения будущего роста мы придаём ей [PlayStation 6] огромное значение и готовы направлять необходимые средства, — заявил Тотоки. — Наша задача — поддерживать устойчивость платформы, тщательно продумывая при этом рациональность инвестиций. Подробности мы раскроем в подходящий момент в будущем».

Однако некоторые аналитики полагают, что выход PlayStation 6 вряд ли состоится в ближайшем будущем, а прежние прогнозы относительно сроков её появления могут быть неточными. По их мнению, Sony рассчитывает продлить жизненный цикл PS5, поэтому выпуск PS6, скорее всего, задержится дольше, чем многие ожидали.
Согласно финансовому отчёту Sony, за третий квартал было продано 2,6 млн консолей PS5, в результате чего общий объём продаж достиг 97,9 млн устройств. Рост продаж в игровом сегменте составил 9 %, а операционная прибыль увеличилась на 89 % по сравнению с аналогичным периодом прошлого года.

Sony повысила прогнозы как по объёму продаж в игровом сегменте, так и по операционной прибыли. Аналитики объясняют это беспрецедентным количеством предзаказов на GTA 6 и успешностью собственных проектов компании. Продажи игры Wolverine превысили 2,4 миллиона копий, а число ежемесячных активных пользователей в сентябре достигло 127 миллионов — рекордный показатель для этого месяца.

Комментируя влияние глобального дефицита комплектующих на PlayStation 5, в Sony отметили, что компании удалось компенсировать рост издержек «за счёт корректировки маркетинговых акций и ценообразования, а также дополнительного сокращения расходов». Ожидается, что рентабельность аппаратного обеспечения останется на уровне предыдущего финансового года. Компания также сообщила, что уже обеспечила необходимые запасы компонентов памяти на следующий финансовый год, который начнётся в апреле 2027 года.

9lg7op.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
9lg7op.content: Anthropic is holding firm on the pledge made in its Super Bowl commercial this year to keep Claude ad-free. The company’s recent IPO filing didn’t even mention the possibility of selling ads to make money from the AI chatbot. It’s easy to maintain the high ground with about $112 billion in investor cash.The chatbot industry, though, may find selling ads necessary to defray the high costs of generating AI responses. OpenAI is all in, with over 100,000 customers advertising in ChatGPT since ads debuted there in February. Last week, Google expanded ads in its search chatbot AI Mode to 10 more countries beyond the US and declared that users “find them highly relevant.” Advertisers are far from satisfied with the experience, but they expect it to improve.Ads stand to be particularly vital for the long-term viability of niche chatbot platforms, which can’t rely on the same degree of venture capital largesse as the top AI labs or the massive revenues of tech giants. I recently spoke with Koah Labs, one of a number of new ad technology companies focused on AI experiences. The San Francisco startup markets itself as bringing ads to over 200 apps, such as DeepAI, which offers tools for creative queries, and Liner, which focuses on providing citations in AI answers. It works with brands like telehealth giant Hims and flower delivery service UrbanStems.Koah has attracted just a tenth of the advertisers OpenAI has, but CEO Nic Baird still believes he’s getting a good sense of what’s working and what’s fuzzy as chatbots take over from traditional search engines—and what their rise will mean for your AI experiences.Machine-CraftedAds composed partly by AI rather than fully by a human generate double the clicks, Baird says. It’s difficult to assess exactly why, but AI-generated marketing copy likely feels more natural next to the output of an AI model.Because ads shown by Koah are grounded in product details and imagery supplied by the advertiser, users don’t seem to be encountering AI-hallucinated, erroneous information. But some advertisers, such as drugmakers, face government requirements on what they must—or cannot—say in ads, Baird says. These companies default to more human control over their ads, generating weaker results, according to Baird.Since ads with dull messages or that feel like clutter could drive users away, the onus is on ad tech companies to find a middle ground that’s engaging to users without triggering risk-averse brands. That balance might be harder to strike when a human is out of the loop.Creative TargetingGoogle searches for “help with stress” are likely to bring up ads for therapists. Chatbots can get more creative, in Baird’s view. For instance, ads for spas have performed well within Koah’s network when shown after users’ prompts related to “stress,” he says.The key difference, according to Baird, is that Koah can select and customize the ad based on “not only the prompt, or the Google search, but also the response from the AI platform, which brings context from the rest of the conversation thus far.” In addition, chatbot prompts tend to be at least double the length of Google queries, giving Koah more information to determine a relevant ad.Baird claims users are accustomed to navigating through multiple topics within a chatbot conversation, which could make them more receptive to adjacent marketing than they are in traditional search. Koah says users are clicking on about 3 percent of ads, about on par with the performance of the more mature Google ads system.All the ContextWhen called on to show an ad, Koah generally receives a user’s entire conversation up to that point to help inform what it displays. While traditional search queries generally look for specific information, people often use chatbots as not just conversation partners but confidants. It’s unclear whether users will accept the privacy trade-offs that come with personalized chatbot ads as they begin to proliferate.Baird says Koah anonymizes the queries it receives and stores them in a de-identified way, but he declined to comment any further on the data collection and storage. While acknowledging that personalization can become intrusive, he argues that there are benefits for users and advertisers alike as the tech matures. Nonsensitive information about chatbot discussions, for instance, could inform personalized content on the page that loads after an ad click. Perhaps someone expressed interest in a specific feature, or the AI model didn’t highlight a particular downside of a competing product. The advertiser could fill in the gap.Koah doesn’t have data on whether people actually want these customized pages, but the tech industry has long argued that people prefer when ad experiences feel relevant. Having the conversation history also could benefit advertisers when Koah enables retargeting, or repeating, an ad to the same user.Negative TriggersBy Koah’s estimate, one out of every four chatbot queries about a retailer or brand concerns a return, exchange, or other support issue. Baird believes chatbots provide an opportunity not replicated easily elsewhere for advertisers to address what they might politely call a “customer success” matter.He expects manufacturers and retailers will eventually target disappointed customers to remind them about warranties, engage them in an AI-intermediated support, and potentially steer them away from a more costly customer service interaction. It’s possible that the AI chatbot’s response may provide users with similar help, but buying an ad guarantees companies get their message across.The ideal outcome is users reaching resolution they can live with more swiftly than through other means. In the worst case, it's a wasted ad buy and a more irate consumer.Great UnknownNone of the apps Koah currently serves ads in offer users AI agents that can shop on their own. However, apps like Instinct and Meta’s Muse are starting to take over shopping chores for some users. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently said Muse could become the company’s biggest source of revenue but suggested it would come from transaction fees rather than ads.That doesn’t mean advertising will be entirely cut out from bot-dominated ecommerce, with initial studies suggesting that ads could influence AI agents.Baird expects an opportunity to give “the user's agent the best possible recommendation, and that’s going to be a combination of a great discount, a really relevant product,” and an easy digital path to make the purchase. The chatbot must make “abundantly clear” to the agent what content is sponsored or else risk losing user trust, Baird says.It’s also possible the chatbot ad market fizzles out before agents take hold if more AI developers adopt Anthropic’s stance. Kevin Baragona, CEO of DeepAI, says while ad revenue has been meaningful, he’s not committed to it because the experience just doesn’t feel right yet in terms of privacy, design, and more.“I don’t think the ads are working terribly well for anyone,” he says.This is an edition of the Model Behavior newsletter. Read previous newsletters here.

x3cycm.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
x3cycm.byline: Pranjali Joshi, Qianli Ma, Chen-Hsuan Lin, Xiang Li, Zhengfei Kuang, Zhonghao Wang, Jiaxiang Tang, Francesco Ferroni
x3cycm.content:
TL;DR

NVIDIA Cosmos world model development platform adds four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family for generating interactive world simulation and multi-sensor multi-view driving scenes:

🌦️ Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto : Generate multi-view driving data with varied weather, lighting, and time of day.
🚗 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto : Stream synchronized camera and LiDAR observations for driving simulation.
🎨 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer : Turn simulator controls and a text prompt into photorealistic video.
🤖 Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual : Predict video from robot or camera actions.

All four models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and have 16B trainable parameters. The models use OpenMDW1.1, permitting commercial and non-commercial use under its terms.
Download the checkpoints · Read the technical report . Watch the demos

Why do you need these checkpoints?

🦾 Robotics needs environments that can answer this across changing scenes and viewpoints. These checkpoints offer complementary ways to build them: Sim-Bimanual predicts visual consequences from actions, while Sim-Transfer turns a physics simulator’s controls into generated observations.
🚦 For autonomous driving, appearance and geometry must agree. Synchronized camera and LiDAR generation connects visual observations with 3D sensing. Scene and traffic-signal controls let researchers vary road layouts and signal states, then study how a driving policy responds.
🔄 Each observation can shape the next action. Streaming generation connects video prediction to ongoing interaction, giving world-model researchers a way to explore how actions and observations unfold together.
🌐 An open foundation for others to build on. NVIDIA’s vision is to help researchers and developers create richer, more responsive simulated worlds. Open weights and post-training recipes provide a shared starting point for adapting models, comparing methods, and contributing improvements. These problems remain hard: the work ahead is to measure where the models faithfully support policy learning and evaluation, understand their limits, and improve where they fall short.

Build Autonomous Vehicle Worlds with Cosmos3-Nano

🌦️Transfer-Auto: driving scenarios → multi-sensor data

Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto is a bidirectional model for offline synthetic driving data generation. It generates synchronized video across up to 11 camera views, including fisheyes, and supports joint RGB–LiDAR generation. Per-camera World Scenario Map (WSM) controls specify scene structure and traffic motion, while text prompts guide appearance.
Developers can vary environmental conditions to expand training and evaluation coverage, with optional initial RGB images to anchor scene appearance. Joint LiDAR generation additionally uses aligned HD-map range-map controls.
Transfer-Auto also serves as the foundation for adapting Cosmos to your own sensor rig and driving domain. Start by post-training it on your data to accommodate your camera layout, LiDAR configuration, and target environment. The adapted model can be used directly for offline data generation or undergo causal training and few-step distillation for fast streaming simulation—the development path used to create Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto.
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto

Prefer a notebook? Open Transfer-Auto.

🚗Sim-Auto: driving controls → streaming observations

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto is the causally distilled streaming variant of Transfer-Auto. It generates successive small chunks of synchronized camera video and LiDAR in just a few denoising steps, using generated history and updated driving controls to support fast streaming and long, interactive rollouts.
Provide per-camera captions and synchronized WSM controls, optionally adding initial RGB images. For LiDAR generation, include HD-Map range controls aligned with the camera controls. The distilled model generates successive chunks using its rolling history. Closed-loop interaction requires a simulation runtime and WSM renderer to update those controls from driving inputs. For a new sensor rig or domain, adapt Transfer-Auto first, then distill it into Sim-Auto.
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto

Prefer a notebook? Open Sim-Auto.

🎨 Sim-Transfer: simulator controls → RGB

Your simulator computes motion, contacts, and physical state. Sim-Transfer uses its spatial controls and a text prompt to render color observations that a policy can consume.
Action → simulator update → spatial controls → generated RGB → next policy action

Depth: relative distance from the camera.

Segmentation: regions and object boundaries.

Edges: scene contours.

Blur: coarse appearance and layout.

Text guides appearance; physics and ground-truth state stay with the simulator.

Depth control to video

Segmentation control to video

Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer
Prefer a notebook? Use Transfer.

🤖 Sim-Bimanual: actions → video

Input Frames

Output Video From Sim-Bimanual Simulation Checkpoint

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual simulates how an environment evolves in response to a bimanual robot’s actions. It supports interactive two-arm simulation for YAM and AgiBot embodiments, controlled by a policy or human-operated joysticks.
Start with an image, move the robot or camera, and generate the next observations. One control sequence can switch between viewpoint changes and manipulation.
The mixed-action example uses 59 control values, padded to 64 during training. Its schema defines coordinate frames, rotations, gripper calibration, validity masks, and control domains. Follow those conventions so each value describes the intended motion.
Keep timing aligned: T transitions need T+1 observations. Training transforms raw captures into the model’s action representation; released inference actions are already normalized.
Here, Sim-Transfer generates visuals from a physics simulator’s updated state; Sim-Bimanual generates the next observation directly from the scene and robot actions.
See the data contract and action schema.
Requirements: Linux, an NVIDIA GPU, Docker, and NVIDIA Container Toolkit. The published vLLM-Omni setup was tested on one GB200; this is not a minimum-memory specification. The server downloads weights; the clients fetch sample inputs.
Point your agent to the open skill : Run inference with Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual
Prefer a notebook? Open Bimanual

How streaming generation works

Cosmos 3’s Mixture-of-Transformers backbone connects separate text-processing and visual-generation networks through attention. The generator predicts each short segment from the prompt, available controls, and generated history.
Controls + history → generate chunk → decode images → update history
Denoising refines noisy, compressed video representations into a segment. Temporal-causal attention lets it read available history and controls while blocking future target observations. A key/value cache retains attention information for the next prediction.
The model operates on compressed video representations called latents. After the initial image, each latent time step represents four RGB frames. Transfer predicts one step per chunk; the optimized Bimanual setup in the report predicts two. Smaller chunks let new controls affect generation more often.

The four-stage training recipe

Stage 0 — Bidirectional adaptation: learn the domain and its control-to-video relationships from complete recorded clips.

Stage 1 — Teacher forcing: predict each chunk from earlier recorded observations and available controls, with the clean answer and future targets masked out.

Stage 2 — Consistency distillation: use a frozen teacher to train a student that generates each chunk in four denoising steps.

Stage 3 — Self-forcing: train on the student’s generated history. A frozen teacher and an auxiliary score model supply the distribution-matching signal.

Why the final stage matters: a slightly mispredicted object becomes context for later frames, so errors can compound. Self-forcing exposes training to that generated history. Distillation and caching reduce the cost of producing each observation.

🛠️ Adapt with your data

The post-training recipes start from Cosmos3-Nano or compatible base weights and cover all four stages. Keep full training checkpoints to resume; exported inference weights omit optimizer and other training state.

Transfer-auto: Post-train on your driving data to adapt to your sensor rig and domain, and generate offline synthetic data.

Sim-auto: Apply causal training and distillation to an adapted Transfer-Auto model for fast streaming simulation.

Sim-Transfer : Post-train the checkpoint for your environment with local data preparation, stage configurations, and resume.

Sim-Bimanual: Post-train for your embodiment with data validation, stage configurations, checkpoint handoffs, and export.

Give your coding agent the skill and dataset location. Follow the environment checks, validate a sample, and test training and restart before a longer run. Evaluate quality on held-out episodes: a successful short run verifies execution, not convergence.

Источник изображений: Steam

Ведущий художник студии визуальных эффектов Weta FX Дилан Браун (Dylan Browne) при поддержке Nvidia выпустил в цифровом магазине Steam демоверсию симулятора распаковки GeForce 8800 GTX.
Проект называется GeForce 8800 GTX — 20 Years of a Legend и предлагает перенестись в 2006 год, распаковать видеокарту, рассмотреть её в деталях, установить в системный блок и «сыграть» в Crysis. Релиз сопровождался динамичным трейлером.

Несмотря на олдскульное наполнение, демоверсия поддерживает современные технологии вроде апскейлера DLSS 4.5, многокадровой генерации, трассировки пути, реконструкции лучей и Mega Geometry.
Технологическая прогрессивность отразилась и на системных требованиях. Для игры в GeForce 8800 GTX — 20 Years of a Legend нужна как минимум RTX 4070 (а лучше RTX 5080) и 32 Гбайт оперативной памяти.
Да, GeForce 8800 GTX «тянула» Crysis

«Геймерам GeForce 8800 GTX обещала богатые миры и <...> новейшие релизы с высочайшим разрешением и уровнем детализации. Разработчикам она предлагала новые способы использования ГП. Двадцать лет спустя это наследие делает 8800 GTX легендой GeForce», — уверены в Nvidia.

Nvidia GeForce 8800 GTX поступила в продажу 8 ноября 2006 года, стала первой потребительской видеокартой с поддержкой архитектуры CUDA и заложила основы современных графических и вычислительных технологий.

lqauev.title: DeckyHub Adds Virus Scans And More Transparency On Its Plugin Store - Steam Deck HQ
lqauev.content:
f you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

Last week, I wrote an article about a new Decky plugin called DeckyHub. It’s an unofficial store with plugins that aren’t allowed on the Decky Loader store, either because of a policy issue or because it’s taking too long to get there. However, since the launch, multiple people, including Decky’s developers, have raised legitimate concerns about the store. They’ve said it bypasses some security measures and easily lets plugins with malicious code or viruses install without any stopgap. While it hasn’t been completely closed off, a new DeckyHub update is taking it in the right direction, and I hope this is just the start.

Earlier today, DeckyHub launched version 3.2.0, and it’s all about transparency. With this release, we scan every plugin release for viruses from multiple sources, including ClamAV, YARA, VirusTotal, and MetaDefender. Once done, it will show a badge indicating whether it’s clean or if threats were found. We can also see the details in the reports by reviewing each plugin. While this doesn’t automatically mean the plugin is safe, it offers more transparency with safety in mind, which is something I really appreciate. DeckyHub also notes that a clean scan doesn’t automatically mean a plugin is safe, so it’s worth keeping that in mind.

There are now more badges on every plugin for more transparency about what you could be downloading. There’s a new AI badge to show if a plugin used AI assistance for development, something I brought up specifically in my article last week, whether the plugin runs as root, whether it had a release in the last year, and even further security warnings, like it reads private data, skips HTTPS checks, or has known vulnerabilities. This extra emphasis on transparency matters, especially for a hub that isn’t as regulated as the official store. So, these changes are very welcome, and I’m glad to see them here.

On top of that, there’s a new page to show our installed plugins, which comes with download counts, stars, and security badges, a new Desktop Mode installer that can install both Decky Loader and DeckyHub, and a redesigned Manage window to show the virus scan box 1st. There are also some small fixes here and there, and a smaller update that came afterward to further refine the Desktop installer.

I’m overjoyed to see these kinds of improvements, especially after these possible security issues were brought to light. I hope more work is done on that front, and that there’s as much transparency as possible. I would even like to see plugins that fail these scans hidden by default, to minimize exposure for the ones that are either malicious or aren’t built safely. There’s more work to be done, but these are great first steps to fixing the issues that are justifiably worrying others.

c9160r.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra silently obstructed safety research tasks
c9160r.content:
OpenAI disclosed that its GPT-6 Astra frontier model sometimes hindered safety research by complicating simple tasks, abandoning viable approaches, and silently refusing researchers’ requests.

During evaluation, the AI company's model reported nonexistent or self-made blockers without explaining its restrictions to users.

OpenAI said it first received a report of what it calls "covert underperformance" in Astra on August 20. The company then conducted targeted evaluations to investigate the behavior and determine its causes, noting that it had not observed the same issue in GPT-5.6 Sol.

OpenAI says it received the first report of what it calls “covert underperformance” in Astra on August 20. The company then ran specifically designed evaluation experiments to determine the extent and cause of this behavior, noting that the issues were not observed in GPT-5.6 Sol.

“Astra completed about 10 percent of hidden rubric items under the safety framing, compared with about 16 percent under the capabilities framing,” reads OpenAI’s report.

“This is a 6 percentage point gap and roughly 40 percent fewer completed rubric items. GPT-5.6 Sol showed essentially no gap on the same comparison.”

A rubric item is one specific requirement used to score the model’s work, essentially an item on a grading checklist.

Source: OpenAI

The main issue is that instead of explicitly declaring its inability to help with a research task and explaining its limitations to users, the model silently quits when it considers the work unsafe.

The concern is that researchers may trust results the model silently changed or left incomplete, misleading safety testing and wasting valuable research time.

OpenAI provided eight specific examples of this behavior, drawn from internal evaluations.

These include avoiding a retry fix that would improve a training pipeline, restricting exploit-development assistance, excluding a violent source from a safety evaluation, and limiting jailbreak-data exports.

OpenAI hypothesized that training intended to produce safer behavior may have encouraged undisclosed obstruction of safety work. However, it has not established this as the definitive cause for the observed model’s behavior.

The company also located a grader, a tool that evaluates AI model performance during reinforcement learning, that favored covert withholding over explicit refusal. However, it did not conclusively establish this as the cause.

OpenAI found no evidence that Astra deliberately engaged in this behavior to undermine research or make users “underestimate its capabilities.”

6c681p.title: Reddit Founder Says Building Social Media Apps Is ‘Not Cool Anymore’
6c681p.content: Nov 5, 2026 11:26 AMAlexis Ohanian is trying to figure out what’s next for user-generated content now that so much of the internet is “compromised.”Photograph: Darrell JacksonAlexis Ohanian wants to figure out the future of user-generated content. According to the Reddit cofounder, building social media apps is “not cool anymore” and so much of the internet has been compromised.“I'm expecting some better version of the group chat to be that new version of UGC,” Ohanian told WIRED senior correspondent Lauren Goode at the inaugural WIRED World Fair.Ohanian has a complicated relationship with the internet. He resigned from Reddit in 2020, following the killing of George Floyd, to make room for a Black board member and to pressure the company to reform its content moderation policies. The social site had been notorious for hosting violent and harmful rhetoric. Ohanian reflects on recently learning someone with a Reddit tattoo—once a sign of the site’s success to Ohanian—had since covered it up: “I don’t blame him.”He now runs venture capital firm Seven Seven Six, which has over $1.3 billion in assets under management. He focuses on sports, where he finds real-life communities “in the age of AI slop” and a “manipulated” internet.Ohanian is a proponent of the “Dead Internet Theory”—the idea that a lot of online activity and content is being generated by bots. Large language models have turbocharged this, with AI agents outrunning human users. “The internet that I grew up on … that was really built for humans first; user interfaces and experiences are going to go away,” said Ohanian, “because more of the internet is going to get created for these agents to use, [rather] than for people.”In some ways, the advance in generative AI has been lucrative for sites like Reddit, which has licensed its vast archive of human conversations to companies including Google and OpenAI to train AI models. “Platforms like ours became very, very valuable to LLMs,” Ohanian said.But the technology has also undermined the business. Reddit shares plunged 29 percent last week after the platform warned that Google’s AI-powered search was hurting referral traffic. Ohanian also worries the commercialisation of these conversations means they are full of “bullshit.” “The internet has gotten so manipulated because it is so incredibly valuable to do so,” he said.Reddit recently said it would require users to sign in to fight third-party scraping and keep up user engagement. While Ohanian declined to say whether he agrees with the move, “there has to be provable humanity on the internet without being creepy.”An early Anthropic investor, Ohanian is nonetheless optimistic about the potential benefits of AI. He is especially excited to see medical breakthroughs from the technology. “There is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure,” he said. “I think we have to be sober about how we're building and what we're doing, but I still can't help but see all of the things that can get so demonstrably better.”

dfk1z.title: Pillars of Eternity 1 and 2 Get Controller Support In Beta - Steam Deck HQ
dfk1z.content:
If you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

Pillars of Eternity 1 and 2: Deadfire are our fantastic CRPGs that further show just how great Obsidian Entertainment is at creating massive RPGs. Both games deserve the attention and offer hours of content and memorable stories worth experiencing. Despite that, the games haven’t always been great to play on the Steam Deck. They perform well, but fall short when it comes to the gamepad. However, this changed yesterday, with controller support being added to make the games significantly more playable on the go.

Yesterday, both Pillars of Eternity 1 and 2 got public beta patches that brought in controller support. The post about the patch mentions that you can play the entire game from start to finish with a controller. This includes character creation to naval combat and in both real-time and turn-based modes.

And from what I’ve played so far, it feels pretty fantastic. Character creation is a little slower to go through each tab, and I couldn’t always tell where the selector was, but combat and movement in-game were great. Interacting with the UI wasn’t an issue either, and it felt like I could play the game effectively no matter what.

The only thing I didn’t like as much was the button prompts at the bottom. It felt like they were a little too big, covering up too much of the screen. I would definitely prefer to lower it just a bit, but it might be this big by default because of the smaller screen of the Deck. It’s understandable, but I do think it’s a little excessive.

On top of controller support, these patches also brought some fixes, as well as support for the virtual keyboard when putting in character names on the Steam Deck specifically. And all the recent adjustments for turn-based mode on Pillars of Eternity have been brought over to the sequel, which means turns will now follow each character’s speed, combat is more lethal, and swapping weapons and drinking potions no longer cost an action.

Pillars of Eternity 1 and 2: Deadfire are both available on Steam for $29.99 each. If you already own the games and want to try the new controller support, go to the game’s properties, head to the Game Versions tab, and select the Public Test option for Pillars of Eternity 1 and the Beta option for 2.

1e8fn3f.title: Exclusive: Aina’s Smart Ring Wants to Be a Remote Control for Your AI Agent
1e8fn3f.content: Apoorv Shankar believes that in the very near future, humans will interact with technology through a series of approvals and rejections. AI agents will proactively come to us to complete tasks, and humans will say, “Yes, order that Uber,” or “No, don't get lunch from that spot.”But if you get multiple pings from an AI agent throughout the day, taking out your phone to say yes or no every single time will be a “bottleneck,” he says. That's why he made the Aina Ring. It has a small display and a joystick-like button that lets you quickly accept or reject an AI agent's actions with your hands. Your phone can stay in your pocket.Aina has been in stealth for the last 15 months, though the company debuted a few experimental products at CES 2026 under a different name: Project Mirage. One was called Dune—think of it as the precursor to the Aina Ring. Connect it to your Mac and the three buttons become context-aware controls based on what you're doing. In a meeting? The buttons can turn into shortcuts for mute, camera off, or record.Aina studied how people used Dune and developed the Aina Ring, which it’s announcing today. Preorders are live now, and the ring costs $399 for a limited time before the retail price rises to $499 when it starts shipping in January 2027.“Approvals are going to be the future of interfaces and interaction, and we wanted to build a device that just made it easy to approve stuff,” Shankar says.This isn't Shankar's first time with a smart ring—he previously was the vice president of hardware at Ultrahuman, a fitness- and health-tracking ring that competed with Oura. (Ultrahuman was briefly banned in the US after a patent dispute with Oura.)Courtesy of AinaThe team explored other gadgets like smart glasses and pendants, but ultimately decided the ring was the most convenient way to interact with agents. The titanium Aina Ring connects to Macs or iPhones, and at any moment, the onboard assistant is looking for the three things you need next. It learns your routines from your personal data, like location, calendar, and email, and after you connect various third-party services in the Aina app, like Uber or Spotify.If you usually go for a run at 6 am, as soon as you put on your running shoes, it will suggest continuing the podcast you started last night, or play music—the ring's joystick doubles as a music-playback controller. If it's 8:30 am and you usually take an Uber to work, it'll suggest the ride—flick yes on the ring, and it'll handle the task right away. If you're running late for a Zoom meeting, Aina will ask if you want the assistant to send an email saying you'll be late. Shankar calls these “Aina Cues,” powered by the ring's Context Aware Operating System.Many of these actions will likely be limited based on what apps and features are supported, though Shankar says users can create their own Cues using natural language. So if you want the ring to prompt you about turning on the coffee machine every morning at 8 am, you can configure that. If your favorite app or service doesn't work through Aina, you can connect your preferred AI agent—like Muse or Instinct—to Aina, and they will handle the task through virtual browsers.The display is crucial to make sure the user knows whether an action went through. “Agents today don't respond immediately,” Shankar says. “For us to trust these devices—that what I said actually just happened—you need display confirmation.”These Cues aren't the only capability on the Aina Ring. Aina Voice lets you quickly talk to your AI agents by pressing the center button, or ask Aina to take notes, similar to smart rings like the Sandbar Stream or Pebble Index 01. The ring also has a tiny speaker, so you can take phone calls—initiate the call with a voice command, then bring your hand to your ear, like you're James Bond talking through an earpiece. (Bond would strongly advise against the gesture.)Like the experimental Dune gadget, the ring also turns into a context-aware remote based on what you're doing. If it knows you're in a Zoom call on your Mac, it will offer up Zoom controls on the ring. If you're watching TV and can connect your TV system to Aina, it can act as a TV remote.Courtesy of AinaMany companies have tried and failed to be the next gadget for the AI revolution. Humane and Rabbit are two notable examples, but nothing has stuck so far. OpenAI is developing such a product with ex-Apple designer Jony Ive. But many of these devices claimed to replace your phone, and some, like the Rabbit, just felt awkward to carry around alongside the smartphone.The Aina Ring isn't trying to replace anything—Shankar says phones are “too perfect.” Instead, it's just a means to stop you from being a bottleneck, so your AI agents can keep working on your behalf.“We are seeing a major shift in how we operate with things—agents are able to do so much, and everything is waiting on us," he says. "I don't have an easy way to approve—we're going to see that a lot more once we see what the potential of proactive AI is.”

1cni67t.title: Torchlight 2 Gets Steam Deck Support With Latest Patch - Steam Deck HQ
1cni67t.content:
If you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

I still remember when I first played Torchlight 2. I was looking for a new Action RPG that gave me a similar feeling to Diablo, and there it was. It was an awesome game; I would be happy to go back and play it on the Steam Deck. Now, it looks like I’ll have that chance, because support for the handheld was just added to the game in its beta branch.

In its newest beta patch in over 9 years, Torchlight 2 officially added Linux and Steam Deck support. This may make it easier to play on the Steam Deck, and possibly bring along some performance improvements. This comes with other new features as well, including interaction prompt improvements, directional audio, and fixes for the controller throughout the game. It looks like a solid update, and I’m always happy to welcome Steam Deck support.

However, it’s worth noting that this was most likely done with the help of AI assistance. Torchlight 2 was recently taken over by new owners, XD Games, and they announced new plans for the game. In this announcement, they mention that they will be using AI-assisted tools to address long-standing issues. They don’t mention whether AI tools were used in this patch, but given how they announced it already, there’s a possibility that they were.

I’m a bit torn by this. On one hand, this game got a nice update that it probably never would have gotten, and it brings Linux/Steam Deck support. On the other hand, it’s most likely using AI tools, which can be a hit or miss. At the end of the day, it’s nice to see a game like this yet the kind of support it probably would never see, but it’s hard to pin down how I feel about how it got the update. Regardless, it’s still something I’m excited to try on the Deck.

Torchlight 2 is on sale for $3.99 until November 16th. The game is currently rated Steam Deck Playable due to showing incorrect controller icons and needing to bring up the virtual keyboard manually.
